place.zh: 体育馆 · 院系杯决赛 · 十二月十九日
place.en: The gym · the cup final · 19 December

setup.zh: 零点六秒，落后一分，大刘伤了，换上来的人罚两个。他翻过那只「0」号纸杯站了起来。头一个，砸在前沿上。还剩一个。
setup.en: Point six of a second, a point down, Big Liu hurt — whoever comes on shoots two. He turns over the cup marked "0" and stands. The first hits the front of the rim. One left.

recap.zh: 决赛最后一罚，他是哆嗦着投的——怕是带着走的，进了。
recap.en: The last free throw of the final he shot shaking — fear is carried, not crushed — and it went in.

zh: 最末那只纸杯，翻过来了。
en: Point six of a second, one point down.
The last paper cup, turned over.

story.zh:
十二月十九日，晚上六点五十二分，新地板的漆味还没散尽。替补席上，阿禾摆好一排纸杯，十二只，杯口朝下，最末那一只写着「0」，自打十一月他崴了脚，就再没翻过来。看台最高一排，葛奶奶戴着蓝布套袖在织袜子；老蔡在第一排举着一块硬纸板：「沈道友稳」。

阿禾往后翻新的一页，翻过十月里一页，他眼尖，看见一行：「沈芒　为什么打球　答：想跑快一点　信一半」。耳朵还没烧完，她已经写下：「12月19日　9/11 起，今天第一百天。」

「一百天怎么了？」

「头两个月长的是神经，手学会了；三个月上下，长的才是身子本身。」她把笔帽按上，「九月十一号，你吐在跑道边上。」

家长群里，他爸发来一张照片：家里那台旧电视放着直播，他爸一条腿架在小板凳上，膝盖缠着护膝。底下两个字：「就位。」

七点跳球。中药学院穿着马氏大药房新送的金字球衣，马小宝在篮下像一堵墙。半场打完，针推落后七分。

第三节，一个球滚出底线，停在沈芒脚边。他弯腰捡起来要递过去——看台上几百双眼睛顺着那个球，一齐落到了他身上。他的手一抖，球滑了出去，弹到裁判的脚面上。

看台上「哄」地笑开了：「零号！上场概率涨到百分之二了！」

他坐回板凳。嘴是干的，喝了水也是干的；手心凉，凉里头还冒汗；场上的声音一阵一阵远了，像有人在慢慢拧小收音机。

第四节，比分一分一分咬回来。最后十秒，六十一比六十二。大刘转身往篮下冲，马小宝横着跨过来，两个人在半空撞在一处。哨响。大刘落地，左脚正踩在马小宝的鞋上，脚脖子往外一拐，抱着脚坐在了地上。

马小宝犯规，罚球两次。比赛时间：零点六秒。

「受伤的不能罚。」雷老师在记录台后头站起来，「换上来的人罚。」

大刘被架过替补席，经过最末那个座位，喘着粗气，只说了两个字：「零号。」

沈芒没动。

他脑子里一下子排出来一串理由，一条比一条体面：手凉；没热身；凑数的，本来就不该上。冒到最后一条，竟是他爸的腔调，九月里视频那头那一句：跑不过，就走。

他的屁股，在板凳上，像是生了根。

他抬起头，看见那一排纸杯。十一只都翻过来了，杯底湿着。最末那一只还扣着，那个「0」字黑黑的，朝着他。

他伸手把它翻了过来，空着喝了一口，放下。然后站了起来。腿是软的，他照样站起来了。

中药那边的看台有人喊起来，跟着十几个人一齐喊，有了节拍：「百分之一！百分之一！」马小宝站在篮下，冲他点点头，声音不高：「慢慢来，零号。」

球在手里，比他投过的两千多个都沉。他拍都没拍，屈膝，抬手——

「当」，砸在篮筐前沿上，弹了出来。

还剩一个。
story.en:
December 19th, 6:52 p.m., and the smell of varnish on the new floor hadn't cleared yet. On the bench, Ahe set out a row of paper cups, twelve of them, mouths down; the last one had "0" on it and hadn't been turned over since he twisted his ankle in November. In the top row of the stands, Granny Ge was knitting socks in her blue cloth oversleeves; in the front row, Old Cai held up a piece of cardboard: "Steady, Daoist Friend Shen."

Ahe flipped to a new page further back, past a page from October, and his sharp eyes caught a line: "Shen Mang  why he plays  answer: wants to run a bit faster  half believed". Before his ears had finished burning, she had already written: "Dec 19  from 9/11, today is day one hundred."

"What about a hundred days?"

"For the first two months, what grows is the nerves — the hands learn. At around three months, that's when the body itself grows." She clicked the cap back on her pen. "September 11th, you threw up beside the track."

In the parents' group, his dad sent a photo: the old TV at home showing the livestream, his dad with one leg propped on a little stool, a brace wrapped around the knee. Below it, two words: "In position."

Tip-off at seven. The College of Chinese Materia Medica wore new gold-lettered jerseys donated by Ma's Pharmacy, and Ma Xiaobao was a wall under the basket. At the half, Acupuncture and Tuina were down seven.

In the third quarter, a ball rolled out over the baseline and stopped at Shen Mang's feet. He bent to pick it up and hand it over — and hundreds of eyes in the stands followed the ball and landed, all at once, on him. His hand shook; the ball slipped out and bounced off the referee's foot.

The stands burst out laughing: "Number Zero! Chance of playing just went up to two percent!"

He sat back down on the bench. His mouth was dry, and stayed dry after a drink of water; his palms were cold, and sweating inside the cold; the noise on the court faded away in waves, as if someone were slowly turning down a radio.

In the fourth quarter, they clawed the score back point by point. Ten seconds left, sixty-one to sixty-two. Big Liu spun and drove for the basket; Ma Xiaobao stepped across, and the two of them collided in midair. Whistle. Big Liu landed with his left foot right on Ma Xiaobao's shoe, his ankle turned out, and he sat down on the floor clutching his foot.

Foul on Ma Xiaobao, two free throws. Time on the clock: zero point six seconds.

"The injured player can't shoot," said Coach Lei, standing up behind the scorer's table. "The sub shoots."

Big Liu was helped off past the bench, and as he passed the last seat, breathing hard, he said only two words: "Number Zero."

Shen Mang didn't move.

A string of reasons lined up in his head at once, each more respectable than the last: cold hands; no warm-up; a number-filler, who shouldn't be out there in the first place. The last one to surface came in his dad's voice, that line from the video call in September: if you can't outrun it, walk away.

His backside seemed to have taken root on the bench.

He looked up and saw the row of paper cups. All eleven had been turned over, their bottoms wet. The last one was still mouth down, the "0" on it black, facing him.

He reached out and turned it over, took a sip from the empty cup, and set it down. Then he stood up. His legs were weak; he stood up anyway.

Someone in the Materia Medica stands started shouting, then a dozen more joined in, and it found a beat: "One percent! One percent!" Ma Xiaobao stood under the basket and nodded at him, his voice low: "Take your time, Number Zero."

The ball in his hands was heavier than any of the two thousand-odd he'd shot. He didn't even bounce it; he bent his knees, raised his hands—

Clang. It hit the front of the rim and bounced out.

One left.

label.en: In four, out six, shoot shaking

exits.means: breathes in four, out six, and shoots the last free throw shaking

refuse.zh: 手还在抖。裁判把球递了回来。
refuse.en: His hands still shake. The referee hands back the ball.

story.zh:
裁判把球收回去，等两边站好。这几秒钟，是规则留给他的。

他不想了，换了一样做：吸四拍，吐六拍，吐得慢得像要把肚子里的东西全倒干净。阿禾十月里说过，这是踩刹车——刹得住一截，刹不干净。手还在抖。可这个动作他在北风里做了两千多回，熟到用不着想；熟了的事，交给身子去做，抖着也做得出来。

耳朵里那层嗡嗡的东西退下去一点，他听见一个声音，很小，很近：场边，阿禾那支笔，「嗒」地按了一下。

她要记了。不管进不进，她都要记。

怕还在那儿，看台上的人一个也没少。可怕，原来不是压下去的，是带着走的。

他拍了两下球，屈膝，抬手。手是哆嗦的，他没等它不哆嗦。

球砸在篮筐后沿，弹起来，落回筐上，沿着铁圈转了一圈，又转了半圈。看台上那声「百分之一」，喊到一半，停了。

它掉了进去。

他还举着手，嘴里冒出两个字，小得只有自己听得见：「成了！」
story.en:
The referee took the ball back and waited for both sides to set. These few seconds were what the rules left him.

He stopped thinking, and did something else instead: in for four counts, out for six, breathing out so slowly it was as if he were emptying out everything inside him. Ahe had said in October that this was stepping on the brake — it would stop part of it, not all of it. His hands were still shaking. But he had done this two thousand-odd times in the north wind, so often he didn't need to think about it; and what you've done that often, you can hand over to the body, and it can do it even while shaking.

The droning layer in his ears receded a little, and he heard a sound, very small, very close: at the sideline, Ahe's pen went click.

She was going to write it down. In or not, she was going to write it down.

The fear was still there, and not one person in the stands had left. But fear, it turned out, wasn't something you pressed down. It was something you carried with you.

He bounced the ball twice, bent his knees, raised his hands. His hands were trembling; he didn't wait for them to stop.

The ball hit the back of the rim, bounced up, dropped back onto it, rolled once around the iron hoop, then half again. The "One percent" from the stands stopped halfway.

It dropped in.

His hands still raised, two words slipped out of him, so quiet only he could hear: "Done it!"
